title: kvcache-tombstone-chain-compaction-and-graded-recovery-runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident runbook and actionable follow-ups for the March 2026 capacity event traced to tombstone chain accumulation in the KV cache. The incident manifested as sustained memory growth followed by eviction storms and degraded tail latency for inference hosts. This ticket consolidates the short-term mitigations, medium-term compaction and throttling changes, and long-term resiliency measurements, including canary rollout and ops playbook entries.
root_cause: Concurrent duplicate-insert path plus a delayed tombstone compaction window caused chained tombstones to accumulate in shard slabs. The chain prevented normal eviction scoring from reclaiming memory due to a compaction ordering bug and created repeated re-insert/evict thrash under load, amplifying memory growth into a capacity event.

2026-03-01T02:19Z - Latency SLO breaches observed for host pool inference-evenset-9; paging alerts triggered.
2026-03-01T02:27Z - Oncall patched temporary write-back-pressure to limit new inserts to affected shards; memory growth slowed.
2026-03-01T03:10Z - Root cause triage: heap dump and slab maps show long tombstone chains in recently compacted segments.
2026-03-01T04:00Z - Emergency mitigation: enabled background aggressive compactor and increased compaction frequency for 2 hours; nodes recovered to steady-state.
2026-03-01T09:00Z - Incident declared resolved; follow-up planning created (this ticket).
mitigations: Immediate: applied conservative write backpressure to ingress paths targeting affected tenant namespaces to stop growth.
Immediate: increased compaction aggressiveness via runtime flag (kvc.compact.window_ms reduced from 60000 to 5000) for emergency window.
Short-term: rolled out a hotfix that prevents duplicate-insert race on the primary insert path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-repo/kvcache/pull/9812).

acceptance_criteria: Compaction code merged and scoring tests pass in CI demonstrating chain lengths bounded under synthetic stress.
Automatic write-throttle policy implemented and verified in staging with load test showing <10% request error increase when throttled.
Metrics and alerts configured in Console; alert runbook documented and tested with pager simulation.
Canary rollout plan defined and executed with two-week observation period and no memory regression observed before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Alpha: feature flag gated compactor change deployed to 10% of capacity on dedicated staging cluster (runtime-1.26-alpha).
Beta: increase to 30% on pre-prod with synthetic duplicate-insert load for 48h.
Canary: 5% production traffic on non-critical tenant pool for 72h with automated rollback if tombstone_chain_length_p95 increases by >10x.
Full: progressive rollout to remaining clusters over 7 days with automated health gates (memory, eviction-rate, tail-latency).
testing_plan: Unit tests for unlinking logic covering multiple chain shapes and concurrent reclaims.
Integration test that forks two inserters into same keyspace to reproduce duplicate-insert race and asserts chain length stays <=2.
Chaos test: restart compactor process repeatedly while writes are ongoing and assert memory plateaus within expected headroom.
Load test: run 24h tenant-level soak with write throttle behavior validated and SLO metrics monitored.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: kvc.tombstone_chain_length_p95 per-shard and per-tenant (exposed to Console).
New alert: Pager if any shard tombstone_chain_length_p95 > 20 for 15m or memory > 80% for 10m without corresponding traffic spike.
Dashboards: Add visualization for compaction throughput, chain length distribution, and eviction vs compaction reclaim curves.
Audit logs: Emit event when emergency aggressive compaction flag is toggled and require SRE approver.

postmortem_summary: A race between duplicate insertion logic and a deferred compaction policy permitted tombstone chains to grow unchecked on a subset of shards. The compactor's ordering bug meant chains were not reclaimed by eviction heuristics, which triggered cascading eviction storms and memory pressure. Emergency throttles and increased compaction frequency stabilized the fleet. This ticket tracks robust compaction, telemetry, throttles, and rollout steps to prevent recurrence.
